title: Reproduction materials: Accurate but Miscalibrated: Testing the Risk Estimates of Medical Machine Learning Classifiers

creators.name: Ebrahim, Ebrahim Khaled
creators.affiliation: Department of Applied Statistics, Faculty of Business, Alexandria University, Alexandria, Egypt

description:
Code, data and results for the paper "Accurate but Miscalibrated: Testing the Risk Estimates of Medical Machine Learning Classifiers" by Ebrahim Khaled Ebrahim.

The study compares nine calibration tests (Hosmer-Lemeshow, Spiegelhalter's z, the Cox slope-and-intercept test, calibration-in-the-large, the GiViTI calibration belt, Osius-Rojek, Stukel, EDGE and a bootstrap test of the expected calibration error) on medical classifiers whose true risk is known: a controlled simulation with known distortions (81,000 replicates), a plasmode simulation on real CDC BRFSS covariates with logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost and a neural network before and after Platt, isotonic and temperature recalibration (1800 replicates), and four public medical data sets.

The deposit holds the Python and R scripts that produce every number, table and figure, the input data, the per-replicate test results, the summaries and the figures. Code is under the MIT licence; results, figures and documentation under CC BY 4.0; the data sets keep their own licences. See README.md for the run order.
